body:
Implements build item 2 of docs/specs/operating-stack.md (§4, §5, §9.2) — the core of the quartermaster layer: a new package `packages/quartermaster` providing (a) the operator-local registry loader and (b) the lifecycle-job routing function `routeJob`, consumed by fleet dispatch. The spec (rev 11+, cross-model reviewed across 11 rounds; read the file as merged on this branch — do not trust cached revisions) is the authoritative contract; §4–§5 define every rule referenced below. The spec is a rail — implement to it, do not amend it in this ticket.

What to build:
1. Registry loader (§4b): loads `quartermaster.json` from an operator-local absolute path outside the repo under review (default: home/XDG; an explicitly configured path that is relative or inside the repo DISABLES loading with a loud notice — mirroring how the adversarial-review CLI treats ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_CONFIG). Load-time validation rules 1–7 (§4b): closed channel names (frontier, frontier-metered, mid, cheap + reviewer groups); adapter must name a module in packages/fleet/lib/adapters/; no command/argv-shaped fields anywhere in the schema; frontier and frontier-metered transports must differ; closed transport taxonomy (subscription:*, api:*, gateway:*); fail closed on any violation — no defaults. Rule 7: the registry carries a `modelProviders` table — (adapter, concreteModel) → normalized provider — covering every model an allowed build alias can resolve to; an alias-based build channel whose adapter has no modelProviders coverage is rejected at load, and modelProviders values must be normalized provider strings. (Phase-2 author binding — a LATER ticket, spec §9.4 — resolves attested concrete models through this table ONLY; this ticket builds the table's schema + validation, not the phase-2 consumer.) Rule 6: reviewer-group members must carry concrete model IDs; build channels may use `default`. The alias contract is ADAPTER-OWNED: each adapter module exports the set of runtime aliases its harness resolves dynamically (at minimum `default` and `latest` where applicable), and the loader rejects a reviewer member whose model matches ANY declared alias of its adapter — not merely the literal string 'default'. Transport validation is a CLOSED taxonomy: a transport whose prefix is not exactly one of subscription:/api:/gateway: is rejected on channels AND on reviewer members (e.g. `proxy:shared` must be rejected, never silently treated as non-gateway — the quorum verifier's gateway discounting depends on this prefix, so an unrecognized prefix passing validation would be a trust-boundary hole, not a cosmetic gap).
2. routeJob (§5): `routeJob({job, assignment, ticket})` — total over the closed job enum, throws on unknown job. For build.* jobs, DERIVE the class: ticket.category in {contract, spec, architecture} → spec-class → frontier; else assignment.float === 0 → critical-path → frontier (overrides assignment tier for channel purposes; tier still governs budget); else ladder-start → assignment tier's channel. assignment.float must be a finite number — absent/non-numeric throws (never default to ladder-start). A caller build.* label disagreeing with the derivation throws. Non-build rows per the §5 table: prosecute.lens → mid; prosecute.verdict → frontier (only overflow-eligible job); review.cross-model.routine/trust-root → reviewer groups; maintain.ratchet/mining → mid; maintain.calibration → frontier-metered; gate.deterministic.* → {deterministic:true}, asserting a channel there is an error.
3. Fleet consumption: fleet dispatch resolves {adapter, model, transport} from the registry via routeJob's channel result and passes the model EXPLICITLY into the adapter invocation (§4c force half; the attest half — resolvedModel — belongs to the adapter ticket, spec §9.3, and is out of scope here). Any registry file found inside the candidate tree is ignored with a notice; dispatch uses only the operator-local file.

Acceptance criteria (spec §12 AC1–AC3, verbatim contracts):
- AC1 isolation: with a registry-shaped file present in the repo AND a valid operator-local registry, a fleet dry-run dispatches per the operator registry and notices the in-repo file was ignored; with the operator path pointing inside the repo, loading is disabled and dispatch fails closed. Verified by `packages/quartermaster/test/registry-isolation.test.mjs` (assert on dispatched argv, notice text, fail-closed exit).
- AC2 validation: fixtures for each §4b rule 1–6 violation (unknown channel name; missing required channel; adapter not in packages/fleet/lib/adapters/; command/argv-shaped key; shared frontier/frontier-metered transport; non-gateway trust-root member lacking directAuth; reviewer member with model 'default' rejected while a build channel with 'default' passes; an alias-based build channel whose adapter has no modelProviders entries rejected vs. accepted with a complete table; a modelProviders value that is not a normalized provider string rejected; a reviewer member whose model matches ANY adapter-declared runtime alias rejected, with one fixture per declared alias of the opencode and codex adapters; an unknown/malformed transport prefix rejected on a channel AND on a reviewer member, e.g. transport 'proxy:shared' and bare 'opencode-go' both rejected naming the closed-taxonomy rule) — each rejected at load naming the rule. Verified by `packages/quartermaster/test/registry-validation.test.mjs` (assert per fixture).
- AC3 derivation: end-to-end test loading a fixture ticket DAG, running @adlc/core computeFloat, feeding assignTicket's ACTUAL output to routeJob (no synthetic float fields on tickets): zero-float ordinary ticket routes frontier even with assignment tier mid; zero-float labeled build.ladder-start throws; category 'spec' labeled build.critical-path throws; absent/non-numeric float throws; unknown job throws; gate.deterministic.* with channel assertion throws; plus a table-driven sweep over every §5 row. Verified by `packages/quartermaster/test/route-job.test.mjs`.
- packages/model-router/lib/assign.mjs is UNCHANGED (rail): its {tier, mode, budget, float} output is consumed as-is.

Out of scope (later tickets per §9): adapter resolvedModel attestation (§9.3), attestation schema v2/quorum (§9.4), telemetry monitors (§9.5). Do not build reviewer-group runtime behavior here — only registry validation of the groups' shape.
title: Build the operator-local channel registry loader and routeJob contract (quartermaster core)
